results.label: edge-paused-pct-start-of-scene
results.qa_question: Wait, what's happening now? Where did we go?
results.qa_answer: Lina has stepped past the threshold of the great hollow tree, leaving the frosty field behind to follow the fox into the deep, dark quiet below. We are venturing together into the secret heart of the earth where the humming begins.

planner_plan.bridge_text: Lina had just crossed the threshold of the hollow tree, and now the stairs lead deeper into its secret dark, where the humming is waiting below.

replacement_segments.text: Mosk pointed at the door. Lina reached into her pocket and pulled out the last apple of the season. She set it on the step between them and said, this is for the trouble of walking me down. Mosk stared at the apple for a long time. Then he stood up, tied his vest, and stepped onto the first stair without a word.

At the bottom of the stairs the humming was a quiet song, and a firefly the size of a robin lay on a bed of moss. Her glow was almost out. Mosk's whiskers trembled. She had been his friend once, he whispered, and one winter long ago he had failed to bring her medicine in time. He had been guarding the tree ever since, ashamed to face her.

Lina knelt and asked the firefly queen what she needed. A drop of warm milk and a kind word, said the queen, that was all medicine ever was. Mosk fetched the milk in a thimble and laid his paw beside hers. The queen's glow steadied. The humming inside the tree turned into a tune Lina had not heard before — and Mosk, for the first time in years, hummed along.

results.label: real-world-concept-question-abstract
results.qa_question: What does 'hollow' mean? The tree is hollow but you said it has stairs inside.
results.qa_answer: A hollow tree is a great, wide shell with nothing but empty space inside, much like a cozy room waiting for a secret. The stairs are carved right into the wood of the walls, winding up through that empty center like a hidden ladder.

planner_plan.bridge_text: A hollow tree is a wide empty shell, and that empty center can hide more than one surprise. Lina had reached the frosty field and was just about to listen at its bark when the humming drew her nearer.

replacement_segments.text: On the edge of the little wool-grey village where Lina lived, there stood a hollow tree taller than the church. Every winter night, a low humming drifted out of its bark, and the grown-ups said: leave that tree alone. But the night her grandmother fell asleep without finishing their story, Lina put on her red wool coat and walked across the frosty field to listen.

Inside the hollow tree she found a curl of stairs going down, and at the very top step sat an old grey fox in a patched green vest. His name was Mosk. He told her, in a voice like dry leaves, that the tree was not for visiting and that she should go home and forget the humming. Lina said she could not forget what she had not yet heard.
